title: Chameleon Room Clip Booth
oneLiner: A browser party toy that turns webcam color-matching and room camouflage into 15-second shareable hide-and-seek clips.
previewUrl: pending Stitch export in Phase B
targetUser: Streamers, friends, students, and portfolio viewers who want a dead-simple physical webcam game that becomes a funny short clip.
keyUx: Use webcam or uploaded room photo, pick a hiding pose, sample background colors, get a camouflage score, and export a 15-second reveal clip card.
spread_trigger: Players post the reveal card because bad camouflage is visibly funny in under 15 seconds.
stitchPrompt: Create a responsive web app called "Chameleon Room Clip Booth" for Streamers, friends, students, and portfolio viewers who want a dead-simple physical webcam game that becomes a funny short clip.. The app is based on observed user pull from S13: A $5 two-person party game about painting yourself to blend into rooms sold 15 million copies in under a month through clip-friendly friend play. S14: Creator videos explain the game in one line: hide-and-seek where players paint their character to match the background. The app should use a Room Camouflage Booth around the trigger moment "Use webcam or uploaded room photo, pick a hiding pose, sample background colors, get a camouflage score, and export a 15-second reveal clip card." and make the first screen communicate "A browser party toy that turns webcam color-matching and room camouflage into 15-second shareable hide-and-seek clips.". Build the core workflow around user-entered evidence and produce 15-second camouflage reveal clip card. Required sections: Webcam room preview; Background color sampler; Pose and hiding zone picker; Camouflage score meter; Reveal countdown; Failure highlight frame; Clip card exporter. Emotional pressure to make visible: 외로움. Toy rule / playable hook: Match the room color, freeze before the reveal, and let friends judge if you disappear. Design direction: use the playful-experimental profile with clip-native party-toy UI with a strong first impression, playful score treatment, and one clear record/export workflow. Avoid generic dashboard framing; make the main interaction feel like Room Camouflage Booth.
